text: Nullable tool parameters (pinnedTime, pinnedEndTime, notes) are declared with type "string|null". The Stavrobot plugin runner type-checks "string" and rejects JSON null, but skips unknown type strings, so this is the only way an explicit null (which the Wherewhen API uses to clear a field) reaches the script. Manifests are JSON and cannot hold a comment.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Rejected: client-side validation of times, legMode and notes length in the tools. The Wherewhen API already rejects bad values with a 400 whose message says how to fix it, and the tools pass that message through, so duplicating the rules would only drift. Observed 2026-09: the API accepts move_stop of a placeholder to index 0 of an empty day (HTTP 200) although the guide says a placeholder cannot be first; add_stop does reject it with 400.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Owner rule (27 Sep 2026): the bot must always switch the plugin's trip_token to work on another trip and must never call the Wherewhen agent API directly. Implemented as the switch_trip tool, not as prose. Rejected: (1) putting the rule in the manifest 'instructions' field, because Stavrobot tells the bot to relay instructions to the user and not follow them; (2) putting it in the plugin 'description', because the owner wants descriptions to be one short sentence (they are in the bot's context on every turn); (3) storing the switched token in a separate state file, because the settings page would then show a token the plugin does not use. Multi-trip support (per-call token or a token list) is a possible later idea, not planned.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
